text.content:
Calling represents a bond between your character and a supernatural entity — a spirit, ancestor, or other manifested power. Most Calling cards channel only a piece of that bond: a claw, a shielding wing, a borrowed sense. You stay in play, playing yourself.

Full Manifestation is different. At greater commitment, your character steps aside and the entity takes their place on the battlefield — using its own combat profile, its own Actions and Reactions, and its own Wound Track. You aren't gaining a second creature standing next to you; you disappear, and it stands where you were.

Eight manifestations are available, gated by your Calling Rank: Familiar or Sprite at Rank 0; add Beast, Phantom, or Golem at Rank 1; add Elemental, Ancestor, or Fey at Rank 2. See The Eight Profiles for each one's stat block.

Play an eligible Calling Action as normal and pay its printed cost. If it hits — or resolves however it resolves — you may then pay an additional toll to fully manifest: burn 3 more Action Dice (2 if you have the Summoner Origin) plus Mana equal to the card's Rank + 1. Dice you already rolled for the card can't also pay this burn, and a Reaction can never trigger a Full Manifestation.

Once you've paid it, open your sheet's header menu (the ⋮ icon, top right) and choose Full Manifestation. Pick the subtype that card's Rider names. Your token immediately swaps to that manifestation's own sheet and stat block for the rest of the Encounter.

The first subtype you manifest into during a fight is locked in for that entire fight — you can dismiss and re-enter that same body as many times as you like, but you can't switch to a different one until the Encounter ends.

You aren't getting a fresh turn. The manifestation picks up exactly where you left off: whatever Action Dice and Reaction Dice you had left are all it has, and any Movement you'd already spent this Turn stays spent. Your own Wounds and Conditions are all still true underneath — manifesting heals nothing.

Your card options shrink to match: only that profile's own 2-3 built-in maneuvers, plus universal Basics like Hide or Strike. Your learned catalogue — every card from every Style you know — is off the table until you return to your own body. Your normal weapon and armor sit out of play too; they add nothing to a profile's own attacks.

To leave voluntarily, open the manifestation's own header menu and choose Return to [Your Name] — this costs 1 Action Die, burned on your Turn. You return to the space you left, and can't manifest again until you play another eligible Calling card.

Each profile has its own Wound Track (3 to 5 boxes, depending on the subtype), completely separate from your own 5 Core Wounds. It's also persistent — because your manifestation lives in Foundry as your own dedicated NPC Actor, any Wounds it takes are still there the next time you manifest that same subtype, even in a later session.

The damage pressure building toward your next Wound (your Resilience buffer) belongs to you, not to whichever body is currently active. It doesn't reset just because you transformed, dismissed, or were knocked out of a manifestation — so switching bodies can't be used to shrug off a hit that's already landed, and you'll never be charged twice for the same one.

Example: you'd already taken 2 points of unresolved damage before manifesting your Golem (Resilience 2). Manifesting itself costs you nothing. A hit for 1 more damage now pushes your total to 3 — 1 point over Resilience — so the Golem takes exactly 1 Wound. If you'd manifested at 0 pressure instead, that same hit wouldn't have caused a Wound at all.

Defeat

If a hit fills a manifestation's last Wound box, it collapses immediately: you're forced back into your own body, you take 1 automatic Wound from the shock, and any part of that hit's damage that didn't fit on the manifestation's track transfers to you as well (Temporary Wounds can absorb either). That specific subtype is marked Broken until Downtime — your other seven remain available. On the manifestation's own sheet, a GM or the player resolves this with the Apply Manifestation Defeat header menu option once its Wound Track is full.

A profile marked Living is a valid target for a living-only effect; one marked Nonliving is not — but it still feels pain, can be restrained, and is affected by mental attacks, magic, and ordinary Conditions like anything else. Being a Phantom doesn't make you incorporeal.

Open any profile directly from the Calling Full Manifestations compendium to read its full stat block and maneuvers, exactly like any other NPC.

The first time a character fully manifests a given subtype, the system automatically creates that character's own persistent copy of the profile and hands the controlling player Owner permission on it — you don't need to drag anything from the compendium yourself. Every later manifestation of the same subtype reuses that same copy, which is what makes its Wound Track actually persist between sessions.

Entering, dismissing, and resolving a defeat are all one click from a sheet's own header menu — the character's token swaps to the manifestation for the duration and swaps back automatically. The only things still tracked by hand are the same ones every other Combat Style Specialty already is: paying the entry cost, and clicking Apply Manifestation Defeat once a Wound Track fills.
